newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee trade slowed by rupiah crisis.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee trade slowed by rupiah crisis.

text.p: Indonesia's coffee trade slowed to a trickle on Monday following a sharp decline in the rupiah against the U.S. dollar and tight supply kept local prices relatively high despite weakness in London, traders said.
They said London futures were expected to open weaker later in the day, with the November contract seen opening unchanged to $10 lower following declines in New York last Friday.

"Players are unable to fix prices because of the rupiah's movements against the U.S. dollar," one trader said. "They don't know which exchange rate to use as it keeps changing. They would rather wait until there is some clear direction."
The Indonesian currency was quoted at a low of 2,980/3,000 to the dollar at 0615 GMT, having depreciated by over 20 percent since the beginning of the year.
The traders said that although theoretically the rupiah's decline should give exporters an edge since exports were denominated in U.S. dollars, but this has not been the case.

"In the first place, there are not much beans in the market because the season is already coming to a close," one trader said. "Secondly, the tight supply is keeping local prices relatively high, while prices in London are weak."
Traders said they estimated there were about 30,000 to 40,000 tonnes of beans in the hands of collectors and exporters.
Collectors form the link between farmers and exporters.

"The collectors are very well informed of what is going on in the market, and they know there will be very little coffee available between now and April (when the next harvest begins)," one trader said. "So, they would rather hold on to their beans."
"As for the exporters, much of the beans sitting in their warehouses have already been committed," he added.

Traders said the tight supply in beans was reflected in some sellers asking for equivalent to prices quoted in London. Under normal circumstances, the local export price is usually between $150-$200 a tonne below London's third month.
Traders said grade four robusta coffee was quoted at 3,950-4,000 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 4,000-4,100 rupiah a week ago.
The export price was quoted at $1,450-$1,500 a tonne exLampung, against $1,550-$1,600. London's November contract fell $26 to close at $1,504 a tonne last Friday.
The traders said Lampung remained parched, with no signs of rains, sparking concern over the flowering process.
"If we are to have a good crop next year, we should have rains in September," one trader said. "There has been no rain in Lampung over the last two months, and this is worrisome."
